Market Sentiment

Phase 1 · domestic EOD evidence from validated local history

How to read the sentiment result Score not ready · run EOD update

The full score is not active yet. Load current EOD data to view the provisional domestic-market reading.

PositiveMost active evidence points to healthier market conditions. Treat this as supportive context, not an automatic buy signal.
MixedThe evidence disagrees or lacks breadth. Review the individual cards before changing portfolio risk.
NegativeMultiple inputs point to market stress. Review exposure and risk controls; this is not an automatic sell signal.

Reliability: fresher data, broader stock coverage and more available evidence clusters make the reading more useful. “Score not ready” means the six-cluster composite is still under development; the domestic reading is provisional.

Candidate v1 weights: cash trend 25% · participation and price strength 20% · volatility 15% · institutional flows 15% · currency and rates 10% · global risk 15%.

Candidate validation: Run the local analysis to evaluate evidence coverage. The candidate label and score remain hidden until validation is complete.

Transition-aware recovery review

Recovering market is assigned from prior regime history only: at least five confirmed weak/high-risk sessions followed by confirmed improvement. It lasts no more than 20 sessions and is evaluated only after the rule is assigned.

Named stress-event review

Each event is compared with non-overlapping windows of the same length outside every named event. A high drawdown or stress percentile means the event was more severe than most ordinary historical windows.

Review windowDatesIndex returnControl median returnReturn percentileExcess vs benchmarkMaximum drawdownDrawdown severity percentileRelative drawdownEntry regimeExit regimeWeak/high-risk sessionsStress percentileRecovering sessionsRecovery percentileFirst weak/high-risk reading
Named-event results will appear with the selected-index validation.
This is a risk-state test, not a direction forecast. A high-risk reading can be followed by a sharp rebound while still containing the worst drawdowns.

Cross-index historical comparison
